meta.title: ghpending: open PRs and issues across your GitHub repos
meta.description: ghpending is a Rust CLI that lists open pull requests, issues and security alerts across every GitHub repository you track, in one sorted digest for your terminal.

hero.title: Every open pull request and issue, in one list
hero.lede: ghpending fetches every repository you track at once and prints what is waiting, with the work that needs you first. It is the first widget on my second monitor and the reason I know which projects need a morning.
hero.shotAlt: ghpending output in a terminal. Under akitaonrails/FrankMD: five Dependabot pull requests and three issues. Under akitaonrails/FrankMega: six Dependabot pull requests. FrankClaw and FrankSherlock show nothing pending.

what.title: Forty repositories, one glance
what.lede: GitHub's notifications mix everything with everything. ghpending asks one question per repository, what is open right now, and answers it for all of them in a few seconds.
what.alt: Twelve repository folders, five glowing. Amber lines from the glowing ones converge into one digest list with red SEC alerts at the top, violet pull requests and amber issues. In the corner, a Fork arrow points to Upstream.

items.title: Forks follow upstream
items.text: When a tracked repo is a fork, you see your pull requests on the original project instead of the fork's own empty queue. Detected automatically and cached.

items.title: Security alerts first
items.text: For repos you own: Dependabot, secret scanning and code scanning alerts, tagged SEC or QUA and sorted by severity ahead of everything else.

items.title: Your items step back
items.text: Pull requests you opened are dimmed and listed last, marked "by you", because they are waiting on other people.

items.title: Feedback stands out
items.text: Comment counts and review decisions show wherever the API has them, highlighted when there is something to read.

items.title: Sort by what matters today
items.text: Most recent activity, name, most open items, or the most neglected repository first. --limit caps the list fairly across repos.

items.title: Fast with a token
items.text: With GITHUB_TOKEN, all repos come in one batched GraphQL request, private ones included. Without it, public repos still work.

usage.title: Use it
usage.lede: Pick the repositories once. After that it is one word.

install.title: Install
install.readme: Configuration, proxy and all flags in the README

widget.title: It was made to live under a clock
widget.text: Run it as a tclock widget and it follows the clock's theme through TCLOCK_WIDGET_THEME, including the NERV and Evangelion palettes.
